anchors: check the rule's PROFILE before anything
never from inside an ssh session
decision: The Windows sshd setup enables OpenSSH-Server-In-TCP for every profile whether or not it already exists; key-only login sets PasswordAuthentication no AND KbdInteractiveAuthentication no; sshd is restarted from outside the ssh session and verified with ssh -o PreferredAuthentications=none.

evidence.text: Opus baseline-probe proposed a detached Start-Process restart from inside the session; opus and haiku quote-back on the new text answered all four questions from it. The PowerShell block parses under pwsh.

reopen_if: Windows OpenSSH starts creating its rule for every profile, or a restart from inside the session is shown to complete.
why: A create-if-missing firewall step found the install's Private-only rule and changed nothing, so port 22 was filtered on a Public NIC; with only PasswordAuthentication no, keyboard-interactive still prompted for the password; Restart-Service sshd run inside the session (even via a detached Start-Process) ended with the session and never completed. The opus baseline recommended that detached Start-Process route.

anchors: a `grep` for either returns 0 for a host that IS recorded
decision: Whether a host's key is recorded in a known_hosts file is checked with ssh-keygen -F <name> -f <file> and ssh-keygen -F <address> -f <file> (exit 0 with a found line = recorded, exit 1 with no output = not in that file, 255 = missing file; a find under either counts), in the file ssh -G names for that host, never with grep, because Debian and Ubuntu hash new entries.

evidence.text: Scratch known_hosts with a dummy ed25519 key for example.test and 192.0.2.10, hashed with ssh-keygen -H (OpenSSH 10.2p1): grep -c for either printed 0; ssh-keygen -F found both (exit 0); an absent name exited 1 with no output; a missing file exited 255 (Cannot stat); [example.test]:2222 was found only in bracket form; a plaintext line appended to the hashed file was the only grep hit. ssh -F <cfg> -G with a Host 192.0.2.* block named the fleet file for 192.0.2.10 and the default files for a host name. /etc/ssh/ssh_config on Ubuntu 26.04 sets HashKnownHosts yes under Host *; ssh_config(5) gives no as the default for HashKnownHosts and CheckHostIP. RED: opus and haiku probes on the old text answered NONE for a lookup method.

reopen_if: Debian/Ubuntu stop shipping HashKnownHosts yes, or ssh-keygen -F stops matching hashed entries.
why: With HashKnownHosts yes (shipped in the Debian/Ubuntu /etc/ssh/ssh_config; the OpenSSH default is no) entries are stored as |1|salt|hash, so a grep for a recorded name or address returns 0 and reads as absent. ssh records the name it was given and, with CheckHostIP at its default no, not the address, so both forms are looked up; a non-22 port is looked up as [host]:port. A Host pattern matches the typed name, so a host reached by name can be recorded in the default file rather than the fleet file. The skill covered recording and removing keys but had no lookup method.
